title: Geometric-stalk perfectness at finite and field coefficients
statement:
Let $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, let $M\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ be a
bounded constructible
complex of finite Tor amplitude
on the coefficient site,
and let $\bar y\to Y$ be a
geometric point.
Then $M_{\bar y}\in D(\Lambda)$ is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded
complex of finite free $\Lambda$-modules. The same conclusion
holds on the small etale site with the corresponding constructibility
and derived-tensor
Tor-amplitude conditions.
Separately, for a bounded constructible complex at a
field coefficient stage
$E$, or in the
common-stage
$\Qlb$-category, its geometric stalk is a bounded complex of
finite-dimensional vector spaces over that field and is perfect.

proof.text: At finite coefficients, use the local quotient coefficient ring and the intrinsic/fixed-module-sheaf equivalence. Transport the given Tor interval to the fixed-sheaf realization. Choose the existing bounded flat model in that interval. Geometric point fibres preserve flat objects, and the canonical fixed/intrinsic stalk isomorphism transports that flatness to the actual finite coefficient stalk. This produces the same finite Tor interval for the stalk.

The exact stalk commutes with homology. Intrinsic constructibility is equivalent to constructibility of the fixed-module realization; descend the latter to a constructible etale sheaf. The canonical comparison of pro-etale and etale geometric stalks makes each cohomology stalk finitely generated. Tor amplitude implies bounded cohomological support. Apply the existing noetherian finite-Tor perfectness theorem and its local-ring finite-free-model API. For the small-etale assertion use the same flat-model argument directly with the lifted etale point; its unlifted/lifted fibre isomorphism transports finite generation.

For an integral representative K, its defining completeness and common reduction interval give a bounded derived-complete integral module stalk by lem-t5-integral-stalk-roos-control. Constructibility of the first reduction gives finite cohomology of its uniformizer cone by lem-t5-integral-stalk-residue-finite. The cone cohomology long exact sequence injects each stalk cohomology modulo the uniformizer into this finite cone cohomology. The ring of integers is adically complete by the existing finite-module completion theorem, transported through ULift. Derived completeness of homology and the complete-ring finiteness criterion now show that all stalk cohomology modules are finitely generated. Localizing the coefficient DVR at its uniformizer is flat. The existing exact scalar-extension cohomology theorem therefore gives bounded finite-dimensional field cohomology. The field perfectness criterion yields the required bounded finite-dimensional model.

Apply the rational assertion at the finite field of definition. Scalar extension along its inclusion into the common coefficient field is exact. Tensoring the bounded finite-dimensional model preserves its degree bounds and finite-dimensional terms. The composition isomorphism for extension of scalars identifies this complex with the fieldGeometricStalkComplex in the common-stage statement, and the exact-derived-functor factorization transports the rational derived isomorphism.
